title: Full dual support or a proper subcurve carrying first cohomology
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes with completed local $k$-algebras $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Cohomology means Zariski module-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and $h^i(X,F)=\dim_k H^i(X,F)$. Let $M$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] with $H^1(X,M)\ne0$. Let $\omega_X$ be the duality module of [lem-sfb-nodal-line-serre-riemann-roch]. At least one of the following holds:
(1) there exists a map $M\to\omega_X$ nonzero at the generic point of every irreducible component;
(2) there is a nonempty proper reduced union $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ of irreducible components, allowed to be disconnected, such that
$$h^1(X,M)=h^1(Y,i^*M).$$
Here the reduced union, closed immersion and restriction use [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-module-pullback]. Irreducible components have the meaning of [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Section 4, Proposition 4.1 proof, printed p.48, first two cohomological-support cases; explicit alternative reconstructed from Serre duality and the annihilator adjunction (Stacks curves.tex Tag 0E33, lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM). Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary text read online.

proof.text: Projectivity makes $X$ proper. Proper-field coherence gives that $X$ is Noetherian and $M$ is coherent; hence $X$ has finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_r$, with generic points $\eta_j$. Nodal Serre duality identifies $V=\operatorname{Hom}_X(M,\omega_X)$ with $H^1(X,M)^\vee$. Thus $0<\dim_k V=h^1(X,M)<\infty$. The field $k$ is infinite: if its underlying set were finite, the positive-degree polynomial $\prod_{a\in k}(T-a)-1$ would have no root, contradicting algebraic closedness.

source.place: Tag 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), (5); properties.tex Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components); preparation for the support argument.

proof.text: For each $j$, let $K_j=\{\varphi\in V:\varphi_{\eta_j}=0\}$. Taking stalks respects addition and $k$-scalars, so these are linear subspaces of $V$. If every $K_j$ is proper, finite linear avoidance gives $\varphi\in V\setminus\bigcup_j K_j$. Its generic stalk is nonzero on every component, proving alternative (1). Otherwise put $S=\{j:K_j\ne V\}$; then $S$ is a proper subset of $\{1,\ldots,r\}$, and every map in $V$ vanishes at $\eta_j$ for $j\notin S$.

source.place: Support case separation by finite linear avoidance; explicit reconstruction of the inference in Franciosi--Tenni Proposition 4.1, printed p.48.

proof.text: If $S$ were empty, each $\varphi:M\to\omega_X$ would have zero stalk map at all component generic points. Reduced-curve duality's generic detection, applied to the coherent source $M$, would give $\varphi=0$. This contradicts $V\ne0$. Thus the reduced union $i:Y=\bigcup_{j\in S}C_j\hookrightarrow X$ is nonempty and proper. The nodal-subcurve theorem gives that $Y$ is projective, reduced, pure of dimension one and nodal, allowing disconnectedness. Projectivity makes $Y$ proper. Pullback preserves invertibility, so $i^*M$ is invertible; proper-field coherence makes it coherent. No connectedness of $Y$ has been used.

source.place: Tags 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), 0BS3 (lemma-duality-dim-1-CM), and 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve); choice of the collective support subcurve.

proof.text: Let $J=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Y)$. The defining-ideal theorem makes $J$ quasi-coherent. The ideal-product theorem makes $JM\subseteq M$ quasi-coherent, and the coherent-submodule theorem makes $JM$ coherent because $X$ is locally Noetherian and $M$ coherent. At a selected generic point $\eta_j$, remove the finitely many other components of $X$. On the resulting neighbourhood $Y$ and $X$ have the same underlying space and both are reduced; the ideal defining $Y$ there has radical zero, hence is zero in the reduced structure sheaf. Thus $J_{\eta_j}=0$ for $j\in S$. For $j\notin S$ the complement of $Y$ is a neighbourhood of $\eta_j$, so $J_{\eta_j}=\mathcal O_{X,\eta_j}$.

Choose $\omega_Y$ with its representing duality from the reduced-curve theorem. Its uniqueness also identifies the chosen nodal $\omega_X$ with the representing module used in closed-subcurve adjunction. For $\varphi\in V$, restrict it to the coherent submodule $JM$. At a selected generic point the source is zero since $J_{\eta_j}=0$; at an unselected one $\varphi_{\eta_j}=0$. Reduced-curve generic detection gives $\varphi(JM)=0$, equivalently $J\varphi(M)=0$. Closed-subcurve adjunction identifies $i_*\omega_Y$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_{\omega_X}(J)$. Thus every $\varphi$ factors uniquely through $i_*\omega_Y$. This gives a $k$-linear isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(i^*M,\omega_Y)\simeq V$: on a trivialization $M|_U=\mathcal O_U m$, a map to the annihilator with $m\mapsto w$ gives the map on $Y$ sending $\bar a\,i^*m$ to the section corresponding to $aw$. It is well-defined since $Jw=0$; uniqueness makes these formulas glue and gives the inverse of composition with the annihilator inclusion.

source.place: Tags 0BS3 (lemma-duality-dim-1-CM) and 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM), (2); annihilator factorization of every dual map.

proof.text:
The reduced-curve duality theorem applies on $Y$ to the coherent module $i^*M$, without a connectedness hypothesis. Proper coherent-cohomology finiteness applies as well, so $H^1(Y,i^*M)$ is finite-dimensional. Duality on $Y$, the isomorphism of step 5, and duality on $X$ give
$$h^1(Y,i^*M)=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_Y(i^*M,\omega_Y)=\dim_k V=h^1(X,M).$$
For a finite-dimensional vector space, its dual has the same dimension (use the dual basis). This is alternative (2) for the nonempty proper $Y$ of step 3.

The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and use the same hypotheses as lem-sfb-nodal-line-serre-riemann-roch. Live and side-live still have the item unsplit, so this is the first delivery, with no repair note and no SGA. Steps: (1) properness, proper-field coherence, finitely many components (Mathlib leaf) and nodal Serre duality give 0<dim V=h1<inf, and k is infinite. (2) The kernels of generic stalk maps are subspaces; finite linear avoidance gives (1) when all are proper, otherwise S is a proper subset. (3) S is nonempty by the generic-detection clause of lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module (source M coherent; the nodal omega_X is identified with the reduced-curve omega by representing uniqueness). The nodal-subcurve node gives Y projective/reduced/pure/nodal, possibly disconnected, and i*M is invertible and coherent. (4) J is quasi-coherent and JM coherent (ideal-times, 01Y1 node); J vanishes at the generic points of selected components (reduced, other components removed) and equals O at unselected ones. (5) phi restricted to JM has zero generic stalks, so phi(JM)=0; closed-subcurve adjunction (0E33(2), curves.tex l.759) gives Ann(J)=i_*omega_Y, and the i*/i_* adjunction gives Hom_Y(i*M,omega_Y)=V. (6) Duality on Y plus finiteness give h1(Y)=dim V=h1(X). Small cases: irreducible X always gives (1); P1 u P1 with bidegree (-2,0) gives h1=1 with every dual map zero on the degree-0 component, so (2) is needed. The parent's step 5 uses exactly alternative (2). No duplicate found (only hit lem-trf-curve-integral-closed-tests, a different statement); no new nodes. The 7 declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. Batch-5: proper-field-invertible-coherent, reduced-curve duality, subcurve annihilator, closed-subcurve adjunction and Euler-characteristic finiteness are coherent algebraic geometry. Their closure hits (field-complex splitting, nodal-subcurve boundary, schematically-dense-open definition) are generic linear algebra, local geometry and definitions. Neither the trace formula nor Poincare duality nor their proofs give any of these, so all are outside the assumptions. Franciosi-Tenni is correctly WANTED; proof_origin by agent.
